For the strongest pair fit an ordinary least-squares line predicting CytoSig z-score from PROGENy z-score on the same matched lines. Report slope, intercept and R-squared, then the twelve cell lines with the largest absolute residual, ties alphabetically. Give their scores, prediction, residual and primary disease from the cell-line metadata, without exporting patient metadata. Draw the correlation heatmap and a score scatter of the twelve largest-residual cell lines with the fitted line, plus residual bars; supply the correlation matrix and the twelve-cell-line table and avoid treating correlated inferred signatures as proof of pathway causality. If a requested ranked list has fewer eligible members, return every eligible member and state the count.

Report slope, intercept and R-squared, then the twelve cell lines with the largest absolute residual, ties alphabetically. Give their scores, prediction, residual and primary disease from the cell-line metadata, without exporting patient metadata. Draw the correlation heatmap and a score scatter of the twelve largest-residual cell lines with the fitted line, plus residual bars; supply the correlation matrix and the twelve-cell-line table and avoid treating correlated inferred signatures as proof of pathway causality. **Limitations**

- Statistical correlation between inferred PROGENy pathway activities and CytoSig cytokine signaling z-scores reflects shared transcriptional response signatures across cell lines and does not establish mechanistic causality, direct cytokine pathway activation, or biological necessity.
- PROGENy and CytoSig z-scores represent computational signature activities derived from downstream transcriptomic profiles rather than direct physical cytokine concentrations or absolute protein abundance.
